text: The Patriots find themselves in genuine crisis mode heading into Sunday's matchup at Buffalo, sitting at 1-2 after a humbling 35-6 loss to Jacksonville in which Drake Maye threw two interceptions and lost a fumble while the offense sputtered to a league-worst 9.7 points per game. Though Maye insists his right shoulder is fine and hasn't affected his throwing ability, he's taking a hard look inward at his own play and the offense's performance, both of which he called "unacceptable," suggesting the real issues go deeper than physical limitations—questions are circulating about whether the Patriots are deploying the young quarterback correctly in the first place. To make matters worse, guard Greg Van Roten landed on injured reserve with a thigh injury Tuesday, further compromising the offensive line infrastructure around Maye, though the team did add some depth by signing rookie offensive lineman Da'Metrius Weatherspoon to the practice squad. The Patriots will need to find answers fast when they travel to Highmark Stadium on Sunday at 1 PM ET to face the Bills.
